name: Whitepages

steps.note: The opt-out page asks for the URL of the profile, so the listing is found first. This is the search the site's own people search in the page header submits, and it takes a name and a location, as its two boxes show. The boxes are visible on the capture; the query string behind them was read from that form's own markup on verified_on.
Two result cards can open the same profile. Reduce the matches to distinct profile URLs and run this manifest once per distinct URL.

selector.label: Copy and paste the URL of your profile

steps.note: The one field on step 1. Its visible text is the instruction inside the box.

steps.prompt: Step 1 of 5. This sends the listing URL to Whitepages and opens step 2. Check the URL in the box, then say yes to send it.

Step 2 of 5 asks Is this the person you want to remove? and shows one listing with a name and an address. Read what is on screen and tell me it is the right person before I click Remove Me. If it is the wrong one, the page has a link under the button that goes back.

steps.note: Step 2 of 5. The page also carries a link reading This is the wrong person. Take me back, which is the way out when the listing is somebody else's.

Step 3 of 5, a required dropdown. The capture shows it closed, so the reasons it offers are not on the image and none is named here. Open it, match the profile's opt_out_reason against what it lists, and if nothing matches, ask the person which of the listed reasons they want. The comment box beside it is marked optional and is left empty.

steps.prompt: Step 3 of 5. The reason you chose is selected and the comment box is empty. This sends the reason to Whitepages. Say yes to continue.

steps.note: Step 3 of 5. The button is greyed out on the capture until a reason is chosen.

Step 4 of 5. The page says the number is used to place a verification call and states it will not be used for any other purpose, which makes it a number the broker rings rather than the number on the listing. It comes from contact_phone for that reason: whoever is running this has to be able to answer it within the minute, and in operator mode that is not always the person whose listing is being removed.

steps.prompt: Step 4 of 5. The number in the box is the one about to go to Whitepages, and it is the one they will ring. Check it, and check that whoever answers it is here.

Whitepages verifies by calling that number, and the call goes out the moment the button is pressed. The box I am about to tick reads: By checking this box I affirm that I am the person associated with this phone number, and I would like my information to be removed from Whitepages listings. That has to be true of whoever answers. Say yes when the person whose number this is has the phone in hand, and they will be asked for a code. If Whitepages refuses the number, stop there and tell me: some brokers will not take a number they read as internet telephony, and the answer to that is a different number you can answer, not the number on the listing.

selector.label: By checking this box I affirm that I am the person associated with this phone number, and I would like my information to be removed from Whitepages listings.

steps.note: Step 4 of 5. Ticked only after the gate above, because the person is the one affirming it.
Step 4 of 5. This places the call. It sits behind the phone_verify gate for that reason.

steps.prompt: Whitepages is now on step 5 of 5, which shows a code to read to the automated caller and then confirms the request. That page has not been captured, so finish it on screen yourself. Tell me what it said and say when the request is accepted.
steps.note: Step 5 is the only one of the five with no capture behind it. Nothing about it is described here. When someone captures it with their values blanked, this handoff is what gets replaced.

verification.success_when: The listing no longer appears in the site's own people search for this name and location. The page says a person can opt out and have their listing removed from the Whitepages website.

additional_captures.of: Step 1 of 5, the public opt-out page again, seen inside a person's guided run on 2026-09-09 and unchanged from source_capture
Step 2 of 5, the listing confirmation card, from that same run with the name and address painted out
Step 3 of 5, the reason dropdown closed and the optional comment box, from that same run
Step 4 of 5, the phone field, the affirmation checkbox, and the Call now to verify button, from that same run with every box empty

id_requirements.note: No account, payment, notarised document, or photo ID is asked for on any of the four captured steps. Step 4 does ask for a phone number and places an automated call to it, which is a gate rather than a document.

notes: Written from five captures: the public opt-out page on 2026-09-08, and steps 1 to 4 as they appeared inside a family member's guided run on 2026-09-09. The run captures are listed in additional_captures. Only step 2 held anything of theirs and it is under solid boxes; the other three were captured with every box empty. Steps 2 to 4 carry no css fallbacks in their selectors, because those pages were read as images and their markup was not. One thing on the step 4 image is not the broker's: a small icon inside the phone box, which is a browser extension's own control and holds no value. Step 5 has no capture and stays a handoff. Three things this manifest says are not on any capture, each stated here rather than dressed up as page text. First, recheck_after_days is 1 with recheck_stated true: the acceptance banner on step 5 states 24 hours, which the person saw in that run and nobody has captured, so the figure is the broker's own and its page is not in this repository yet. Second, a terms and cookie consent dialog stands in front of the site's search results, and one of its controls opened a Premium checkout in a new tab during that run; no accept_terms step is written because the dialog was not captured, and capturing it needs a browser profile that has not seen it. Third, two result cards resolved to one profile URL in that run, which is why find_listing reduces by URL before anything is filled. Four submit gates appear because Whitepages sends something on each of its first four pages, and each gate approves the values filled since the one before it. What the first capture shows and what it does not: the heading, the step marker, the sentence, the field, the button, and the site's own people search are all on the image; the css fallback in the step 1 selector and the search query string were read from that page's own markup on the same visit, and the image holds no browser address bar, so home_url, source_url, and optout_url record addresses that were open rather than anything legible on it.
